config.title: flex-grow, shrink, basis

intro.title: flex-grow, shrink, basis
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a flexible card layout that adjusts to different screen sizes using CSS Flexbox. You will learn the core concepts of flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis, which control how flex items expand, shrink, and set their initial size within a container. The main technologies involved are CSS Flexbox properties, applied to HTML elements styled in a CSS file. By the end, you'll understand how to create responsive designs that adapt smoothly, making your web pages look great on any device.
intro.usecase: The flex-grow, shrink, and basis properties are essential for creating responsive layouts that adapt to different screen sizes and content. In real-world applications, you'll use them to build dynamic navigation bars where menu items expand or shrink to fill available space, or in dashboard panels that resize proportionally when the window is adjusted. For example, in a data table, you can set columns to have a flexible basis so they grow to show more content or shrink to prevent overflow, ensuring a clean, user-friendly interface across devices.

objectives: Apply the flex-grow property to control how flex items expand to fill available space
Configure the flex-shrink property to manage how flex items contract when space is limited
Initialize the flex-basis property to set the default size of flex items before distribution
Construct a flex container with items that demonstrate different growth and shrinkage behaviors
Manipulate the flex shorthand property to combine grow, shrink, and basis values
Update existing layouts by adjusting flex properties to achieve responsive sizing
Integrate flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis to create balanced, adaptable flexbox layouts

steps.title: Create a container with display: flex
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a .container class that sets display: flex
steps.hint: Start by writing .container { } and inside the curly braces add the display property with the value flex.
steps.seedCode: /* Create a .container class with display: flex here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A .container CSS rule is created with display: flex, establishing a flex container.
successCriteria: The .container rule exists and includes display: flex.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have .container { display: flex; } exactly.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a .container class with display: flex.

steps.title: Add three child divs with basic styling
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules for three child elements (.item1, .item2, .item3) with width: 100px, height: 100px, background-color: lightblue, and margin: 10px.
steps.hint: Create three separate CSS rules, one for each class (.item1, .item2, .item3), each containing the same four properties: width, height, background-color, and margin.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create a .container class with display: flex here */

/* Add CSS rules for .item1, .item2, .item3 here */
steps.expectedOutcome: Three CSS rules are created for .item1, .item2, and .item3, each with the specified width, height, background-color, and margin properties.
successCriteria: CSS rules exist for .item1, .item2, and .item3, each containing width: 100px, height: 100px, background-color: lightblue, and margin: 10px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created some of the required CSS rules, but not all three items have the complete set of properties. Make sure .item1, .item2, and .item3 each have width: 100px, height: 100px, background-color: lightblue, and margin: 10px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rules for the three child elements are missing or incomplete. You need to create three separate rules for .item1, .item2, and .item3, each with width: 100px, height: 100px, background-color: lightblue, and margin: 10px.

steps.title: Set initial flex-basis values for all items
steps.instruction: Add the flex-basis property to each .item class with different pixel values: 100px for .item1, 150px for .item2, and 200px for .item3.
steps.hint: Use the flex-basis property to set the initial main size of each flex item. Add it inside each existing .item rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each flex item will have a different initial size before any growing or shrinking occurs.
successCriteria: All three .item classes have flex-basis properties with the specified pixel values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added flex-basis to some items, but make sure all three have the specified values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added flex-basis properties with the correct pixel values to all three .item classes.

steps.title: Apply flex-grow to make items expand
steps.instruction: Add flex-grow properties to the three .item classes to make them expand proportionally when there's extra space. Use values like 1, 2, and 3.
steps.hint: Add flex-grow: 1; to .item1, flex-grow: 2; to .item2, and flex-grow: 3; to .item3. This will make them grow at different rates.
steps.expectedOutcome: The three flex items will now expand proportionally when the container has extra space, with .item3 growing the most and .item1 growing the least.
successCriteria: All three .item classes have flex-grow properties with different values (1, 2, 3).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some flex-grow properties, but make sure all three items have them with values like 1, 2, and 3.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-grow properties aren't correctly added. Check that each .item class has a flex-grow property with appropriate values.

steps.title: Remove flex-grow and apply flex-shrink
steps.instruction: Remove the flex-grow properties from all three .item classes and add flex-shrink properties with values 1, 2, and 3 respectively.
steps.hint: Replace each flex-grow declaration with flex-shrink and assign the same numeric values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The three items will have flex-shrink values set instead of flex-grow, preparing them to demonstrate shrinking behavior when the container is too small.
successCriteria: All three .item classes have flex-shrink properties with values 1, 2, and 3, and no flex-grow properties remain.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but check that all three items have flex-shrink properties and no flex-grow properties remain.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't match the expected changes. Make sure to remove flex-grow and add flex-shrink with values 1, 2, and 3 to the respective items.

steps.title: Combine flex-grow and flex-shrink
steps.instruction: Add flex-shrink properties to all three .item classes while keeping their existing flex-grow values. Use different shrink values for each item (e.g., 1, 2, 3).
steps.hint: Add a flex-shrink property to each .item rule, placing it after the flex-grow property. The values should be different for each item to see how they shrink differently.
steps.expectedOutcome: All three .item classes will have both flex-grow and flex-shrink properties with different values, allowing them to both expand and shrink when the container size changes.
successCriteria: Each .item rule contains a flex-shrink property with a distinct value, and all items retain their existing flex-grow properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some flex-shrink properties, but check that all three .item classes have them with different values, and that the flex-grow properties are still present.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't yet show flex-shrink properties added to all items with different values while maintaining their flex-grow properties. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Use the flex shorthand property
steps.instruction: Replace the individual flex-grow and flex-basis properties in .item1, .item2, and .item3 with the flex shorthand property in the format flex: [grow] [shrink] [basis]. Use flex-shrink: 1 for all items.
steps.hint: The flex shorthand combines flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis in that order. For example, flex: 1 1 100px;
steps.expectedOutcome: The three .item classes should use the flex shorthand property instead of separate flex-grow and flex-basis properties.
successCriteria: All three .item classes use the flex shorthand property with the correct grow, shrink, and basis values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but some items still use separate properties instead of the flex shorthand. Make sure all three .item classes use flex: [grow] [shrink] [basis];
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex shorthand property wasn't implemented correctly. Remember to replace both flex-grow and flex-basis with a single flex property in each .item class.

steps.title: Create a flex item that doesn't shrink
steps.instruction: Modify the .item2 rule to prevent it from shrinking by setting flex-shrink: 0.
steps.hint: Add flex-shrink: 0; to the .item2 CSS rule to make it maintain its size when the container shrinks.
steps.expectedOutcome: The second flex item (.item2) will maintain its size and not shrink when the container width decreases.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added flex-shrink: 0; to the .item2 rule. Check that the syntax is correct.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .item2 rule should include flex-shrink: 0; to prevent it from shrinking. Try adding this property to the existing .item2 CSS rule.

steps.title: Create a flex item with fixed basis
steps.instruction: Update the .item3 rule to use a fixed flex-basis of 200px while keeping its flex-grow value.
steps.hint: Change the flex-basis value for .item3 to 200px to make it a fixed width, while the other items will use their current basis values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The third flex item will have a fixed starting width of 200px, while still being able to grow proportionally with the other items.
successCriteria: The .item3 rule has flex-basis: 200px and flex-grow: 3.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure .item3 has both flex-basis: 200px and flex-grow: 3. The flex-basis should be exactly 200px (fixed value).
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're updating the .item3 rule correctly. It should have flex-basis: 200px and flex-grow: 3. This creates a flex item with a fixed starting width that can still grow.

steps.title: Experiment with different container widths
steps.instruction: Add a width property to the .container class to observe how flex items respond to different container sizes.
steps.hint: Try setting a specific pixel width or percentage width on the container to see how the flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis properties affect the items' sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have a defined width, allowing you to see how flex items grow, shrink, or maintain their basis when the available space changes.
successCriteria: The .container class includes a width property with a valid CSS value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a valid width value to the .container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container width hasn't been properly set. Add a width property to the .container class with a valid CSS value.
